business_problem: GSK needs to extract actionable disease insights from rapidly growing genetic, genomic, clinical, and health datasets so it can predict patient risk and treatment response, prioritize experiments, and improve the speed and success rate of drug and vaccine R&D.
solution_summary: GSK is using an in-house AI and machine learning stack to analyze large-scale genetic, genomic, clinical, and health datasets for drug discovery and patient stratification. The implementation combines GSK’s historical clinical archives with external datasets such as UK Biobank, including genome sequencing data and electronic health records, through a single platform that gives researchers pooled access to data resources. In-house algorithms and machine learning models are used to identify patterns in biological data, predict future patient responses to potential medicines, estimate who is at risk of developing diseases such as hepatitis B, and identify lupus patients least likely to respond to traditional treatments. GSK also runs a lab-in-the-loop reverse translation process in which engineers, geneticists, and biologists use active learning pipelines to rank hypotheses and targets, test them experimentally, and feed results back into the models for additional prioritization.

solution_components.name: machine learning models
solution_components.role: Predict future patient responses, disease risk, and carrier likelihood for conditions including chronic hepatitis B.

solution_components.name: active learning
solution_components.role: Drives lab-in-the-loop pipelines that prioritize experiments and refine hypotheses using experimental feedback.

solution_components.name: UK Biobank
solution_components.role: Supplies large-scale genetic, genomic, and linked health data that GSK uses to augment internal research datasets.

data_flow: GSK combines internal clinical archives with external sources such as UK Biobank genome data and linked electronic health records in a single platform. Machine learning models and in-house algorithms analyze these pooled datasets to predict disease risk and treatment response, while active-learning lab-in-the-loop pipelines prioritize experiments; experimental results are then fed back to guide further research and clinical trial decisions.
business_outcome: GSK reports that AI and machine learning are already helping predict patient responses and disease risk, narrow research toward higher-need disease areas, and reduce research and development costs by cutting the time and resources needed to make progress on new medicines and vaccines.
